# Create Compose UI Component
## When to Use When the user asks to create a new reusable UI component (button variant, card, dialog, list item, etc.) that should live in `:core:ui-library`.
## Location All reusable components go in: `core/ui-library/src/main/kotlin/sk/styk/martin/apkanalyzer/core/uilibrary/components/<Name>.kt`
## Template
```kotlin package sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.uilibrary.components
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier import androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Preview import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.uilibrary.theme.ApkAnalyzerTheme import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.uilibrary.theme.AppTheme
@Composable fun <Name>( // Required parameters first (no defaults) label: String, onClick: () -> Unit, // Optional parameters with defaults modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, ) { // Wrap the Material3 component, applying theme colors // Use AppTheme.colors and AppTheme.typography for consistent theming }
@Preview @Composable private fun <Name>Preview() { ApkAnalyzerTheme { <Name>( label = "Sample", onClick = {}, ) } }
@Preview @Composable private fun <Name>DarkPreview() { ApkAnalyzerTheme(isDarkTheme = true) { <Name>( label = "Sample", onClick = {}, ) } } ```
## Rules
### Component Design - Wrap `androidx.compose.material3` components — feature modules must NOT use material3 directly. - Apply theme colors from `AppTheme.colors` (e.g., `AppTheme.colors.primary`, `AppTheme.colors.surfaceVariant`). - Apply typography from `AppTheme.typography` (e.g., `AppTheme.typography.labelLarge`). - Use shapes from `sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.uilibrary.theme.Shapes`. - `Modifier` parameter is always present with default `Modifier`.
### Parameter Ordering 1. Required state parameters (text, data) 2. Required callback parameters (`onClick`, `onValueChange`) 3. `modifier: Modifier = Modifier` 4. Optional parameters with defaults
### Callback Naming - Use present tense: `onClick`, `onValueChange`, `onDismiss` - Never past tense: ~~`onClicked`~~, ~~`onChanged`~~
### Previews - Every component file MUST have `@Preview` functions. - Wrap all previews in `ApkAnalyzerTheme { }`. - Preview functions are `private` and suffixed with `Preview`. - Use realistic sample data — no empty strings or placeholder text. - Preview multiple states: default, selected, disabled, dark theme.
### Immutable Data Classes If the component takes a data parameter, define it with `@Immutable` or `@Stable`: ```kotlin @Immutable data class <Name>Item( val id: String, val label: String, ) ```
### Collections Use `ImmutableList` from `kotlinx.collections.immutable` for list parameters: ```kotlin @Composable fun <Name>List( items: ImmutableList<<Name>Item>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, ) ```
## Existing Component Reference Available components in `core:uilibrary:components`: `AppIcon`, `BottomSheet`, `Button`, `Checkbox`, `Chip`, `DateRangePickerDialog`, `Icon`, `IconButton`, `LoadingSpinner`, `NavigationBar`, `RangeSlider`, `SearchBarActive`, `SearchBarInactive`, `SkeletonBox`, `Switch`, `Text`, `Toolbar`

# Create Core Module
## When to Use When the user asks to create a new core/shared library module for domain logic, data access, or reusable utilities.
## Steps
Given a core module name `<name>` (e.g., `app-export`):
### 1. Create build file
**File: `core/<name>/build.gradle.kts`**
Without Hilt (pure utility module): ```kotlin plugins { alias(libs.plugins.apkanalyzer.library) }
android { namespace = "sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.<flatname>" }
dependencies { implementation(projects.core.common) } ```
With Hilt (has repositories/managers with DI): ```kotlin plugins { alias(libs.plugins.apkanalyzer.library) alias(libs.plugins.apkanalyzer.hilt) }
android { namespace = "sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.<flatname>" }
dependencies { implementation(projects.core.common) } ```
> `<flatname>` is the module name without hyphens. Examples: > - `app-export` → `appexport` > - `analytics` → `analytics`
### 2. Create repository interface + implementation (if applicable)
**File: `core/<name>/src/main/kotlin/sk/styk/martin/apkanalyzer/core/<flatname>/<Name>Repository.kt`** ```kotlin package sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.<flatname>
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
interface <Name>Repository { fun data(): Flow<List<Model>> suspend fun getById(id: String): Model? } ```
**File: `core/<name>/src/main/kotlin/sk/styk/martin/apkanalyzer/core/<flatname>/<Name>RepositoryImpl.kt`** ```kotlin package sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.<flatname>
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.flow import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.flowOn import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.common.coroutines.DispatcherProvider import javax.inject.Inject
class <Name>RepositoryImpl @Inject constructor( private val dispatcherProvider: DispatcherProvider, ) : <Name>Repository { override fun data(): Flow<List<Model>> = flow { // implementation }.flowOn(dispatcherProvider.io())
override suspend fun getById(id: String): Model? = withContext(dispatcherProvider.io()) { runCatching { /* ... */ }.getOrNull() } } ```
### 3. Create Hilt module (if using DI)
**File: `core/<name>/src/main/kotlin/sk/styk/martin/apkanalyzer/core/<flatname>/di/<Name>Module.kt`** ```kotlin package sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.<flatname>.di
import dagger.Binds import dagger.Module import dagger.hilt.InstallIn import dagger.hilt.components.SingletonComponent import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.<flatname>.<Name>Repository import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.<flatname>.<Name>RepositoryImpl import javax.inject.Singleton
@Module @InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class) internal interface <Name>Module { @Binds @Singleton fun bind<Name>Repository(impl: <Name>RepositoryImpl): <Name>Repository } ```
### 4. Register in `settings.gradle.kts`
Add inside the `include(...)` block: ```kotlin ":core:<name>", ```
## Rules - Core modules never depend on `feature` modules. - Core modules can depend on other core modules (always depend on at least `core:common`). - Public interfaces are non-throwing: use `Result<T>`, `T?`, or empty collections. - Use `DispatcherProvider` for all dispatcher switching. - Use `@Singleton` scope for repository/manager bindings. - Interface + `Impl` pattern: interface for public API, `Impl` class with `@Inject constructor`.
## Namespace Mapping Examples | Directory | Namespace | |-----------|-----------| | `core/apps` | `sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.apps` | | `core/app-permissions` | `sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.apppermissions` | | `core/user-preferences` | `sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.userpreferences` | | `core/ui-library` | `sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.uilibrary` |

# Create Feature Module
## When to Use When the user asks to create a new feature, screen, or feature module.
## Steps
Given a feature name `<name>` (e.g., `about`):
### 1. Create API module
**File: `feature/<name>/api/build.gradle.kts`** ```kotlin plugins { alias(libs.plugins.apkanalyzer.feature.api) }
android { namespace = "sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<name>.api" } ```
**File: `feature/<name>/api/src/main/kotlin/sk/styk/martin/apkanalyzer/feature/<name>/api/<Name>NavKey.kt`** ```kotlin package sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<name>.api
import androidx.navigation3.runtime.NavKey import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
@Serializable object <Name>NavKey : NavKey ```
If the NavKey needs parameters, use `data class` instead: ```kotlin @Serializable data class <Name>NavKey(val id: String) : NavKey ```
### 2. Create impl module
**File: `feature/<name>/impl/build.gradle.kts`** ```kotlin plugins { alias(libs.plugins.apkanalyzer.feature.impl) }
android { namespace = "sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<name>.impl" }
dependencies { api(projects.feature.<name>.api) // Add core module dependencies as needed: // implementation(projects.core.apps) // implementation(libs.kotlinx.collections.immutable) // implementation(libs.coil.compose) } ```
### 3. Create entry provider
**File: `feature/<name>/impl/src/main/kotlin/sk/styk/martin/apkanalyzer/feature/<name>/impl/navigation/<Name>EntryProvider.kt`**
If the feature does NOT need navigation (no `navigator` calls): ```kotlin package sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<name>.impl.navigation
import androidx.navigation3.runtime.EntryProviderScope import androidx.navigation3.runtime.NavKey import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<name>.api.<Name>NavKey import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<name>.impl.<Name>Screen
fun EntryProviderScope<NavKey>.<name>Entries() { entry<<Name>NavKey> { <Name>Screen() } } ```
If the feature DOES need navigation (back, or to other screens): ```kotlin package sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<name>.impl.navigation
import androidx.navigation3.runtime.EntryProviderScope import androidx.navigation3.runtime.NavKey import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.navigation.Navigator import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<name>.api.<Name>NavKey import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<name>.impl.<Name>Screen
fun EntryProviderScope<NavKey>.<name>Entries(navigator: Navigator) { entry<<Name>NavKey> { <Name>Screen( onBack = { navigator.goBack() }, ) } } ```
### 4. Create screen composable (placeholder)
**File: `feature/<name>/impl/src/main/kotlin/sk/styk/martin/apkanalyzer/feature/<name>/impl/<Name>Screen.kt`** ```kotlin package sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<name>.impl
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxSize import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier import androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Preview import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.uilibrary.components.Text import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.core.uilibrary.theme.ApkAnalyzerTheme
@Composable internal fun <Name>Screen() { Box( modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize(), contentAlignment = Alignment.Center, ) { Text(text = "<Name>") } }
@Preview @Composable private fun <Name>ScreenPreview() { ApkAnalyzerTheme { <Name>Screen() } } ```
### 5. Register modules in `settings.gradle.kts`
Add these lines inside the `include(...)` block: ```kotlin ":feature:<name>:api", ":feature:<name>:impl", ```
### 6. Add dependency in `app/build.gradle.kts`
Add inside the `dependencies` block: ```kotlin implementation(projects.feature.<name>.impl) ```
### 7. Wire entry provider in `app/src/main/kotlin/sk/styk/martin/apkanalyzer/ui/ApkAnalyzerApp.kt`
Add import: ```kotlin import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<name>.impl.navigation.<name>Entries ```
Add inside `entryProvider { }` block: ```kotlin <name>Entries() // or: <name>Entries(navigator) if it uses Navigator ```
### 8. If top-level destination (bottom nav)
Add to `app/src/main/kotlin/sk/styk/martin/apkanalyzer/ui/navigation/TopLevelDestinations.kt`: - Import the NavKey and add a new `NavigationBarItem` to `TOP_LEVEL_DESTINATIONS` - Choose icons from `ApkAnalyzerIcons` - Add string resource to the api module's `res/values/strings.xml`
## Naming Rules - Module directory: kebab-case (`app-detail`) - Gradle accessor: camelCase (`projects.feature.appDetail.impl`) - Package: concatenated lowercase (`feature.appdetail.impl`) - NavKey class: PascalCase + `NavKey` suffix (`AppDetailNavKey`) - Entry provider function: camelCase + `Entries` suffix (`appDetailEntries`)

# Implement Navigation to a Screen
## When to Use When the user asks to add a new screen/destination within an existing feature module, or wire navigation between features.
## Scenario 1: Add an internal screen within a feature
Internal screens are sub-destinations within a feature (e.g., filter screen within apps feature).
### 1. Create internal NavKey
**File: `feature/<feature>/impl/src/main/kotlin/.../navigation/<Name>NavKey.kt`** ```kotlin package sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<feature>.impl.navigation
import androidx.navigation3.runtime.NavKey import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
@Serializable internal data object <Name>NavKey : NavKey ```
If the NavKey needs parameters: ```kotlin @Serializable internal data class <Name>NavKey(val id: String) : NavKey ```
### 2. Create the screen composable
**File: `feature/<feature>/impl/src/main/kotlin/.../<subpackage>/<Name>Screen.kt`** ```kotlin package sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<feature>.impl.<subpackage>
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
@Composable internal fun <Name>Screen( onBack: () -> Unit, // other callbacks ) { // Screen content } ```
### 3. Register in entry provider
Add to the existing entry provider function in the feature's `navigation/<Feature>EntryProvider.kt`:
```kotlin entry<<Name>NavKey>( metadata = slideFromEndEntryMetadata(), // or bottomEntryMetadata() ) { <Name>Screen( onBack = { navigator.goBack() }, ) } ```
If the NavKey has parameters, access them via the `key` lambda parameter: ```kotlin entry<<Name>NavKey>( metadata = slideFromEndEntryMetadata(), ) { key -> <Name>Screen( id = key.id, onBack = { navigator.goBack() }, ) } ```
### 4. Navigate from source screen
In the source screen's entry in the entry provider, add navigation callback: ```kotlin onNavigateTo<Name> = { navigator.navigate(<Name>NavKey) } // or with parameters: onNavigateTo<Name> = { id -> navigator.navigate(<Name>NavKey(id)) } ```
## Scenario 2: Navigate to another feature's screen
Cross-feature navigation uses NavKeys from `feature/*/api` modules.
### 1. Add API module dependency
In the source feature's `build.gradle.kts`: ```kotlin dependencies { implementation(projects.feature.<target>.api) } ```
### 2. Navigate using the target's NavKey
In the entry provider: ```kotlin import sk.styk.martin.apkanalyzer.feature.<target>.api.<Target>NavKey
// Inside the entry block: onNavigateToTarget = { navigator.navigate(<Target>NavKey) } // or with parameters: onNavigateToTarget = { id -> navigator.navigate(AppDetailNavKey(AppDetailInput.InstalledPackage(id))) } ```
## Transition Types
Available transition metadata functions from `core:uilibrary:animation`:
| Function | Use For | |----------|---------| | `slideFromEndEntryMetadata()` | Detail screens, sub-screens pushed onto stack | | `bottomEntryMetadata()` | Bottom sheets, filter panels | | No metadata (default) | Top-level tab destinations | | Custom `NavDisplay.predictivePopTransitionSpec` | Special transitions (e.g., search overlay fade) |
## Entry Provider Patterns
### Without Navigator (self-contained screen, no navigation out) ```kotlin fun EntryProviderScope<NavKey>.<feature>Entries() { entry<<Feature>NavKey> { <Feature>Screen() } } ```
### With Navigator (navigates to other screens or back) ```kotlin fun EntryProviderScope<NavKey>.<feature>Entries(navigator: Navigator) { entry<<Feature>NavKey> { <Feature>Screen( onBack = { navigator.goBack() }, onNavigateToDetail = { id -> navigator.navigate(DetailNavKey(id)) }, ) } } ```
### With NavKey parameters (assisted injection ViewModel) ```kotlin entry<<Feature>NavKey>( metadata = slideFromEndEntryMetadata(), ) { key -> <Feature>Screen( input = key.someParameter, onBack = { navigator.goBack() }, ) } ```
## Wiring Checklist - [ ] NavKey created (`@Serializable`, implements `NavKey`) - [ ] Screen composable created - [ ] Entry registered in entry provider with appropriate transition metadata - [ ] Navigation call added in source screen's entry block - [ ] Entry provider wired in `ApkAnalyzerApp.kt` (only for new features, not internal screens) - [ ] Cross-feature: API module dependency added in `build.gradle.kts`

# Spotless Fix
## When to Use When the user reports formatting errors, ktlint violations, or asks to fix code style. Also run after generating or modifying Kotlin files to ensure they pass CI checks.
## Commands
### Fix all modules ```shell ./gradlew spotlessApply ```
### Fix a specific module ```shell ./gradlew :<module>:spotlessApply ```
Examples: ```shell ./gradlew :app:spotlessApply ./gradlew :core:apps:spotlessApply ./gradlew :feature:apps:impl:spotlessApply ```
### Check without fixing (dry run) ```shell ./gradlew spotlessCheck ```
### Check a specific module ```shell ./gradlew :<module>:spotlessCheck ```
## Spotless Configuration
The project uses ktlint with these custom rules (configured in `SpotlessPlugin.kt`):
| Rule | Setting | |------|---------| | Multiline function signatures | Forced when 3+ parameters | | Compose CompositionLocal allowlist | Disabled | | Compose lambda-param-in-effect | Disabled | | Function naming for `@Composable` | Ignored (PascalCase allowed) |
### Custom ruleset `io.nlopez.compose.rules:ktlint` — Compose-specific lint rules for ktlint.
## Common Violations and Fixes
### Multiline function signature ```kotlin // ❌ Wrong: 3+ params on one line fun myFunction(param1: String, param2: Int, param3: Boolean) { }
// ✅ Correct: each param on its own line fun myFunction( param1: String, param2: Int, param3: Boolean, ) { } ```
### Wildcard imports ```kotlin // ❌ Wrong import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
// ✅ Correct import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.map ```
### Trailing commas ```kotlin // ❌ Wrong: missing trailing comma in multiline fun myFunction( param1: String, param2: Int )
// ✅ Correct fun myFunction( param1: String, param2: Int, ) ```
### Compose callback naming ```kotlin // ❌ Wrong: past tense onClicked: () -> Unit onItemSelected: (String) -> Unit
// ✅ Correct: present tense onClick: () -> Unit onSelectItem: (String) -> Unit ```
## After Running Spotless
If `spotlessApply` cannot auto-fix an issue, manually check: 1. Import ordering (alphabetical, no wildcards) 2. Blank lines between functions 3. Trailing commas in multiline parameter lists 4. Composable function parameter ordering (`Modifier` after required params)
